description: IAM Access Analyzer Unused Access Tracking Period Longer Than _ARG_0_ Days
rationale: The tracking period is how long a role, password, access key or permission must sit unused before the analyzer reports it, so it is also how long a credential that nobody uses any more stays available without anything pointing at it. A long period is chosen to keep the findings quiet, and it does: a role belonging to a decommissioned workload or a person who has left is reported only once the whole period has elapsed, and every permission granted for a one-off task keeps its reach in the meantime. The period cannot make a used permission disappear from the findings either way, because the analyzer measures actual access, so a shorter one costs review effort rather than correctness.
remediation: Lower the tracking period of the unused access analyzer to the interval within which a legitimately used credential is certain to have been used at least once, and work the resulting findings
